cards.text: Right before this, the prophet watched the whole earth get shaken, and then saw the LORD of Hosts reigning on Mount Zion. Now he stops and talks straight to God: "O LORD, You are my God! I will exalt You; I will praise Your name." He says God has worked wonders, in perfect faithfulness.

cards.question: The prophet says God's wonders came from plans. When does he say those plans were formed?

cards.text: Then he points to a fortified town, a fortress of strangers, and says God has made it a heap of rubble, a city no more. Friend, that's not a town anymore. That's a pile of rocks with a zip code.

cards.question: The prophet says the fortress of strangers will be rebuilt someday.
Because God turned that fortress into rubble, what does the prophet say a strong people will do?

cards.text: Then the prophet tells God why. God has been a refuge and a stronghold.

cards.question: Who does the prophet say God has been a refuge and a stronghold for?

cards.text: He says God has been "a refuge from the storm, a shade from the heat." The breath of the ruthless is like rain against a wall, like heat in a dry land, and God subdues the uproar of foreigners.

cards.question: As the shade of a cloud cools the heat, the song of the ruthless is ___.

cards.text: Then the scene changes: on this mountain, the LORD of Hosts will prepare a lavish banquet of aged wine, choice meat and finely aged wine. A FEAST?! Friend, I'm standing here in my apron holding a cookie box like, "Y'all need dessert? I'm just ASKING."

cards.question: Who is the LORD of Hosts preparing this lavish banquet for?

cards.text: And He's not done. On this same mountain, He will swallow up the shroud that enfolds all peoples, the sheet that covers all nations.

cards.question: After the shroud, the prophet says God will swallow up ___ too.
The prophet says God swallows up death only for a little while.
With death swallowed up, what does the Lord GOD wipe away from every face?

cards.text: He will also remove the disgrace of His people from the whole earth, and the prophet seals it: "For the LORD has spoken." That's not a "we'll see," friend. That's DONE.
In that day, people will say it out loud: "Surely this is our God".

cards.question: In that day, what do the people say they've been doing for the LORD?

cards.text: They waited, He saved them, and now they rejoice and are glad in His salvation. Friend, I waited YEARS in a junk drawer and I'm STILL not over getting pulled out, so I can't even imagine this day.

cards.question: The hand of the LORD will rest on this mountain. But Moab, a nation east of the Dead Sea, will be ___ in his place.

cards.text: Then the prophet says, "He will spread out his hands within it, as a swimmer spreads his arms to swim."

cards.question: The prophet says his pride will be brought low despite something. What?
At the end, the high-walled fortress is left standing tall.

cards.text: It's brought down, cast to the ground, into the dust, and friend, I lived under dust for years. Pride never got anybody out of there; somebody had to reach in.

findings.problem: The opening card states facts from Isaiah 24 (the earth shaken, the LORD of Hosts reigning on Mount Zion) but gives no reference for them. The card cites only Isaiah 25:1.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: "The prophet watched the whole earth get shaken, and then saw the LORD of Hosts reigning on Mount Zion" tells Isaiah 24's prophecy as something already seen happening. Isaiah 24:23 says the LORD of Hosts "will reign" on Mount Zion, so the card changes a future event into a past one.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "Just that morning" is flippant and doesn't match the tone of "Long ago," so the right answer stands out. The wrong answer "After the city fell" points to a city the baker hasn't heard about yet.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: Card 4 has just established that the fortress will never be rebuilt. That rules out the wrong answer "Rebuild the city" before the baker picks.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: No card ever mentions the second half of Isaiah 25:3, that the cities of ruthless nations will revere God. The ruthless come back in verses 4 and 5, so the baker misses this detail.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: "Then the prophet tells God why. God has been a refuge and a stronghold." is a bare summary with none of Papa Dorin's voice. Stop 1 has only one joke in nine cards (card 3), and cards 1, 6 and 8 read flat.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: This story card carries three beats: God as refuge and shade, the breath of the ruthless being like rain against a wall and heat in a dry land, and God subduing the uproar of foreigners.

rule.text: Aim for one beat per story card. Two is the most. If a story card has more than two things happening, split it.

findings.problem: "In that day, people will say it out loud: "Surely this is our God"." is only a quote, with no voice and nothing that carries the moment.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: "Now they rejoice and are glad in His salvation" states that the people rejoice. In Isaiah 25:9 they say "Let us rejoice and be glad in His salvation," which is a call to rejoice, not a report that they are rejoicing.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: Moab is introduced inside a choice card as "a nation east of the Dead Sea." That is a fact from outside the passage and has no reference. A choice card cites only the verses of its right answer, so it has no place to give that reference.
findings.question: When a new person or place is first introduced inside a choice card's question, where should the reference for that outside fact go? Or must every new person or place be introduced on a story card first?

findings.problem: The rest of Isaiah 25:10, Moab trampled "as straw is trodden into the dung pile," is never told. It is the main picture of the verse.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: This card is only a quote, with no voice and no context about who is spreading out his hands or what that means for Moab.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: The question says "his pride" without naming Moab. "His" points back to cards the baker can no longer see.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.
